title: Florida House, District 59
what_it_does: Represents District 59 (Part of Pinellas) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings.

candidates.name: Berny Jacques
candidates.occupation: Attorney (former prosecutor and civil litigator); state representative for District 59
candidates.background: Seminole-area Republican elected to the Florida House in 2022. A former prosecutor and civil litigator with degrees from Washington Adventist University and Stetson University College of Law, he was appointed by Gov. DeSantis to the 6th Circuit Judicial Nominating Commission. He says affordability is the state's most important issue.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: He voted for HJR 1-F and has publicly defended Amendment 3, saying local governments have other places to cut and accusing the City of Largo of using public safety as a scare tactic against the measure.
property_tax.quote: The city was going to use public safety as a scare tactic to get folks to vote against property tax relief.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HJR 1F (Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes), passage 75-26
Jacques weighs in on Amendment 3 after Largo town hall (Florida's Voice)
Sparks fly during Tampa Bay town hall debate over property tax-cutting Amendment 3 (Creative Loafing Tampa)

immigration.summary: Voted yes on SB 2-C (2025), which created the State Board of Immigration Enforcement, required state help with federal detainers, barred driver licenses for unauthorized immigrants, and funded an Unauthorized Alien Transport Program.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, SB 2-C (Immigration), passage 85-30

abortion.summary: Voted yes on SB 300 (2023), the law that limits most abortions after six weeks of pregnancy.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, SB 300 (Heartbeat Protection Act, six-week abortion limit), passage 70-40

guns.summary: Voted yes on HB 543 (2023), which allows carrying a concealed firearm without a state license.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HB 543 (concealed carry without a license), passage 76-32

education_choice.summary: Voted yes on HB 1 (2023), which removed income limits and enrollment caps so state scholarship funds can follow any K-12 student to private or home education.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/CS/CS/CS/HB 1 (universal school-choice scholarships), passage 83-27

crime.summary: A former prosecutor, he says public safety starts with backing law enforcement and that government should never cut public-safety funding.
crime.quote: Public safety starts with backing the men and women, backing the blue, the people who do this job day in and day out.

sources.title: Rep. Berny Jacques touts SunCoast PBA endorsement, backs property tax proposal (Florida's Voice)
Berny Jacques for Florida House (campaign website)

growth.summary: Jacques said he voted for the current law letting counties and cities ban data centers in their communities, which also bars data centers from passing energy costs to consumers and includes water protections.
growth.quote: I proudly voted for the current law that allows counties and cities to ban data centers in their communities.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

healthcare.summary: Asked how Florida should handle Medicaid, Jacques said the focus should be on waste, fraud and abuse rather than on changing eligibility.
healthcare.quote: We should focus on fixing any waste, fraud and abuse in the program.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

energy.summary: Voted for CS/CS/HB 1645 (2024), the 2024 energy law that removed climate change as a priority of state energy policy, repealed several renewable-energy goals and grant programs, banned offshore wind turbines in state waters and eased regulation of natural-gas pipelines; a vote for it is coded as leaning against promoting renewable energy.

candidates.name: Susan Leff
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Marketing, sales and business development consultant
candidates.background: Largo resident with more than 40 years in marketing, sales and business development who now works in networking and consulting. A graduate of Largo High School, St. Petersburg Junior College and the University of South Florida, she was adopted at five days old and describes herself as not a career politician.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

abortion.summary: She says personal medical decisions belong to individuals, not politicians, and emphasizes a woman's right to choose.
abortion.quote: Personal medical decisions belong to individuals — not politicians.

sources.title: Susan Leff for the People - Issues

environment.summary: She says pollution and unchecked development have put waterways and coasts under pressure and calls for coastline protection and clean-water investment.
environment.quote: Pollution, unchecked development, and lack of accountability have put our waterways, air quality, and coastal ecosystems under growing pressure.

sources.title: Susan Leff for the People - Issues

veterans.summary: She proposes ending veteran homelessness, expanding mental-health support and ensuring quality health care for veterans.

sources.title: Susan Leff for the People - Issues

healthcare.summary: Leff told the Times Florida should expand Medicaid and close the coverage gap, with simpler enrollment and taxpayer oversight.
healthcare.quote: Florida should expand Medicaid, not cut it.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

insurance.summary: Leff said she would work to lower property-insurance costs, increase insurer transparency, and oppose unjustified utility rate increases, with public reporting on results.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

housing.summary: Leff said she would fully fund affordable-housing programs, and would spend a $1 million appropriation on a District 59 housing-stability initiative covering emergency rent and mortgage assistance, rehabilitation of affordable housing, and homelessness prevention.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

growth.summary: Leff said Florida should require strong oversight of AI and data centers, with employment guarantees, a municipal bond or comparable financial guarantee, community input and independent oversight.
